title: Signal Sprint: Data Drift
premise: Guide a glowing courier signal across unstable floating data platforms in a neon cyberspace route, stabilizing one node after another before the path becomes too chaotic.
interaction_model: Mobile-first touch action with drag steering on the left side of the screen and tap-to-jump on the right side, presented through a full-screen canvas with overlay HUD and modal result screens.
objective: Cross each generated route of floating platforms without falling and reach the finish platform to stabilize the current node.
progression: Node-based progression with level numbers increasing after each win; routes become longer and, after node 5, noticeably harder with wider gaps, narrower landings, and more side-to-side drift.
theme: Futuristic cyber-network courier run in a glowing digital void.
mood: Arcade-tense, sleek, energetic, and slightly high-alert in later stages.
likely_audience: Players who enjoy simple pick-up-and-play mobile platform challenges, endless-runner style reflex games, and neon sci-fi arcade presentation.
confidence_notes: High confidence that the game is a level-based platform-jumping runner because movement, jumping, collisions, finish platforms, and level generation are explicit in code.
High confidence in the mobile touch control interpretation because the pointer handling splits the screen into joystick and jump zones.
Moderate confidence on whether it should be labeled more as a platformer or runner; the strongest grounded description is a 3D platform runner with discrete stages.
recreation_prompt: Create a mobile-first neon sci-fi arcade game called 'Signal Sprint: Data Drift' where the player controls a cute glowing courier signal moving through a pseudo-3D cyberspace made of floating rectangular platforms. Use a full-screen canvas with a sleek HUD, start screen, game-over screen, and victory screen. The core loop should be: start a node, drag on the left side of the screen to steer the avatar with a virtual joystick, tap on the right side to jump, cross gaps between floating platforms, avoid falling into the void, and reach a bright finish platform to clear the node and advance. The player should have momentum-based movement with friction, capped speed, gravity, grounded jumping, landing feedback, and a camera that follows from behind to create a forward sprint perspective. Generate each level procedurally as a chain of platforms moving away on the Z axis, with a large safe starting platform, many normal platforms with random widths, depths, gaps, and sideways offsets, and a large finish platform at the end. Make progression node-based so each win advances to the next node; after node 5, increase difficulty with wider gaps, narrower platforms, and more aggressive side-to-side route drift, and show a visible 'Red Alert' difficulty badge. Present the world with glowing grid-floor illusions, cool blue and cyan tones in early levels, and harsher red-magenta danger lighting in harder levels. The player avatar should look like a small expressive signal cube with a face, glow, and antenna-like signal crown. Include background music, jump, land, UI, win, and fail sounds, small particle bursts on jumps, and celebratory or failure reaction overlays. Keep the overall tone slick, arcade-readable, fast to restart, and optimized for touch play on phones.
